newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - "Neutral" API data sparks mild selling.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - "Neutral" API data sparks mild selling.

text.p: This week's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) sparked a round of light selling Wednesday evening amid mostly neutral responses from traders who saw supply and demand largely in balance.

The selling impetus was provided by a surprisingly large if still seasonal build in distillate stocks as well as a build in crude stocks which was fueled by imports that surged to 8.93 million barrels per day (bpd).

On the other side of the ledger, market players marveled with guarded bullishness at the fact that gasoline stocks fell as robust implied demand of nearly 8.7 million bpd easily absorbed imports that came in at a rather high 603,000 bpd.

"It's not clearly bearish or bullish. The distillate number is bearish but the gasoline is comparably bullish. The crude build is somewhere in the middle," said Tim Evans, analyst at Pegasus Econometric.
"If gasoline falls it will be because the gasoline draw was not sufficient enough to counter the distillate build," Evans said.
API said distillate stocks rose by 3.3 million barrels last week to 101.7 million, and futures traders on ACCESS pushed the spot June heat contract down about 0.09 cent to 55.40 cents a gallon.
June gasoline on ACCESS stood about 0.05 cent above the earlier close of 65.80 cents a gallon, buttressed by the 1.12 million barrel draw in gasoline that brought stocks to 196.8 million barrels.

"Demand is pretty good in gasoline, but with (refinery) operations up near 97 percent it all looks neutral. Supply and demand seem to be very very much in balance," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst at Cargill Investor Services in New York.
Refinery run rates came down a bit more than expected by 0.9 percentage point to 96.7 percent of total U.S. crude oil distillation capacity, the API report said.
The decline in refinery utilization rates was reflected to some extent in crude stocks, which rose by nearly 1.4 million barrels to 316.1 million.
On the crude front, the API also said it revised week-ago crude stocks downward to 314.7 million from the 315.8 million barrel level originally reported.
July crude dipped 5 cents in early ACCESS action from the earlier close $20.79 a barrel.
Overall, some traders said that despite the report's neutral flavor, the data may be interpreted bearishly since the market has been under downward pressure in recent sessions.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
